glosses: To issue forth, as water from the earth; to flow; to spring.

examples.text: [Blood] welled from out the wound.
[Yon spring] wells softly forth.

glosses: To have something seep out of the surface.

examples.text: Her eyes welled with tears.

glosses: To gradually or steadily flow upwards or outwards so as to begin to fill or overflow something.

examples.text: Oil was welling up out of the borehole.
As soon as I heard news of his death, tears started to well up in my eyes.
A spring wells up in the centre of the village, and watercress beds lie beside the stream running alongside the main street.

glosses: To accumulate within one, to the point of overwhelming one.

examples.text: Emotion welled up inside me.

A barely audible groan welled up in the Captain's throat as the grinning Freedom Fighter circled around behind the helpless American Soldier. The groan sputtered into a strangled, "No… no… don't.... " as Randall felt the juicy tip of the man's tumescent cock jab against his hair-ringed, virgin asshole.
“I had to leave my job because I just couldn’t … yeah,” Tina says, welling up.

glosses: Well versed; well acquainted (in or on).

examples.text: How well up are you on algebra?

glosses: To boil to such an extent as to overflow its container.

examples.text: I forgot about the rice and it boiled over.

glosses: To reach the point where aggressive action is taken.

examples.text: He b'iled right over, and the tongue-lashing he give that boss Right Liver beat anything I ever listened to. There was heap of Scriptur' language in it, and more brimstone than you'd find in a match factory.

But as the half progressed, Liverpool's pressure and high-tempo passing game increased United's frustration and it threatened to boil over on the stroke of half-time when Van Persie, who had already been booked, was involved in angry verbal exchanges with several Liverpool players, particularly Gerrard.

glosses: To act aggressively angry.

examples.text: He boiled over all night.

glosses: To buck aggressively.

examples.text: The stallion boiled over, throwing Robert from her back.

glosses: A traditionally Maori soup/stew made with potatoes, pork and other ingredients.
To cook or prepare by boiling.

examples.text: Can you boil up the vegetables while I baste the meat?

glosses: To become more excited, intense or exciting.
To boil clothes to clean or sanitize them.
